主要内容: Senators Bernie Sanders, Elizabeth Warren, and Tammy Baldwin have urged BlackRock CEO Larry Fink to intervene in a coal miners' strike at Warrior Met Coal. The senators requested that Fink use BlackRock's significant financial stake in the company to pressure management into negotiating a fair contract with the striking workers. The miners are demanding better pay and benefits due to the dangerous working conditions. BlackRock holds approximately 13% of Warrior Met Coal's stock, making it the company's largest shareholder. The senators emphasized the need for BlackRock to publicly demand that Warrior Met negotiate in good faith. The timing of the letter was strategic, as BlackRock was set to release its quarterly earnings report. The strike, which began in April 2021, has been ongoing since the company's restructuring in 2016, when miners agreed to a pay cut and reduced benefits. Sanders criticized the company for not restoring promised compensation and called on Fink to act morally. Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren have urged BlackRock CEO Larry Fink to intervene in a coal strike, continuing a pattern of pressuring Wall Street leaders to support workers. This is not the first time the senators have targeted major investors, as Sanders previously wrote to Warren Buffett, CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, to support striking steelworkers at Special Metals, a subsidiary of Buffett's conglomerate. BlackRock, which manages over $9 trillion, is the largest money manager globally, giving Fink significant influence. Fink has made climate change a central political cause, encouraging companies to reduce carbon emissions and align with a net-zero economy. In 2021, he called for companies to disclose plans for compatibility with a net-zero economy and to adjust investment processes to align with climate goals.
